column1: The Hypothesis Friedman suggested that we view current income Y as the sum of two components, permanent income YP and transitory income YT. That is, Y 5 YP  YT. Permanent income is the part of income that people expect to persist into the future. Transitory income is the part of income that people do not expect to persist. Put differently, permanent income is average income, and transitory income is the random deviation from that average.
